summary: Sets which files Tailwind scans for class names and defines the app's named colors, fonts, animations, and blur.
purpose: Controls the design choices: palettes, fonts, and motion names.
why: Likely reason: named colors let the look be changed in one place. Comments point to docs for the Bain and Nothing palettes.
how: It lists the source files to scan. Inside the extended theme, it sets two named palettes (a Bain red and grey set and a Nothing green, black, and grey set), a monospace and a sans font, four animation names with matching motion steps, and a small blur size.
inputs: The source files, which Tailwind scans at build time.
outputs: Generated class names for colors, fonts, and animations that components can use.
risks: Two palettes overlap: green and orange are each defined under two names. The color named border replaces the default border color for the whole app, and the stylesheet depends on that. Animations are defined both here and in index.css.
debug: If a new class has no effect, check that its file is in the content list. If a color looks wrong, check the palette names here and whether the stylesheet overrides it.
